module: Define the system and its compliance boundary

lesson.title: Separate classification, dates and parallel duties
lesson.summary: Separate classification, application dates, transition and parallel law.

prerequisites.reason: Annex route affects the Sections 1–3 date. A classification conclusion must be separated from other duty triggers.

blocks: A **duty application date** tells you when a particular provision becomes applicable. Classification and date are separate findings. In the 27 July 2026 amended baseline, Chapter III Sections 1–3 apply to Annex III systems from **2 December 2027**, and Annex I systems from **2 August 2028**, subject to the stated exceptions.
Use the current Article 113 and actual route. Do not use the original 2026/2027 high-risk timetable from an older slide. The Article 6(5) guidance duty has a separate exception.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 4, 5, 50, 111(2), 113; amended 2026/1744 baseline

blocks: A **legacy transition** can affect high-risk systems placed on the market or put into service before the relevant date. Article 111(2) ties application to significant changes in design from that date; public-authority intended use has the specified 2030 compliance endpoint.

This is not unlimited permission for any old product. Record initial supply/service date, route, design changes and public-authority use; check the exact transition. A marketing claim of “existing system” does not establish these facts.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 4, 5, 50, 111(2), 113; amended 2026/1744 baseline

blocks: **Parallel obligations** use their own triggers. Most Article 5 prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025; inserted 5(1)(ba)/(bb) and 5(1a)/(1b) have the 2 December 2026 date. Article 50 generally applies from 2 August 2026, with a targeted 50(2) transition for systems placed on the market before that date until 2 December 2026.
Article 50 concerns interaction and specified synthetic content; a notice does not legalise an Article 5 forbidden practice. Data protection and sector or national rules also remain separate checks.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 4, 5, 50, 111(2), 113; amended 2026/1744 baseline

blocks: The amended Article 4 requires providers and deployers to support development of AI literacy among staff and others operating systems on their behalf. Literacy concerns knowledge for informed use; the Act does not create a universal training certificate.

Dossier method: keep one row per actor and duty, with trigger, date, transition evidence and current action. A future high-risk date is not a conclusion that no present obligations exist. All dates in exercises use the stated baseline.
